metrics.duration_note: 14/103 READY deploys sampled via get_deployment (Aug 3–10). Sorted samples: 428.8, 497.2, 514.8, 523.4, 524.6, 529.5, 534.3, 535.9, 540.0, 542.3, 548.3, 550.7, 553.2, 1156.8s. p50=535s (avg positions 7–8 of 14: (534.3+535.9)÷2). p95=765s (0-based idx 12.35: 553.2+0.35×603.6; elevated by single outlier dpl_EdgkBgv9H3XuASvVXkUxTDE8PEi5 at 1156.8s — the W32 observability-snapshot deploy, first build of the window). total_build_minutes estimated as (mean_sample=570.0s÷60)×103_READY=979min. alerts: duration_p50=535s > 360s RED threshold. Build times remain structurally elevated — Turbopack + large Next.js content site averaging ~525s/build (excl. outlier). Marginal increase vs W32 p50 of 512s (+4.5%). Same root cause: no build-time reduction shipped this week. Needs to fall below 360s to exit RED.

duration_p95=765s, up +44.9% vs W32 (528s) — technically RED by the +30% delta rule. Driven almost entirely by a single outlier: dpl_EdgkBgv9H3XuASvVXkUxTDE8PEi5 (1157s, the W32 observability-snapshot deploy at window start Aug 3). Excluding this outlier, p95=553s vs 528s (+4.7%) — not a signal. The outlier is a valid data point but should not be read as a trend.

count_error=1 (down from 29 in W32, -96.6%). Dramatic recovery: 29 ERROR-state deploys last week vs 1 this week. W32's error spike appears resolved (likely by the reading-site self-ingestion fix). count_error==1 is YELLOW by threshold but does not override the p50-driven RED verdict.

count_total=135 vs W32's 244 (-44.7%): lower-velocity week with 31 production deploys and 104 preview builds. total_build_minutes=979 vs 1294 (-24.3%) — proportionate to the volume drop. The p50 remaining above threshold despite lower total volume confirms the elevated build-time ceiling is structural, not load-driven.
